chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
I asked him about the one who divorces [his wife] during a state of purity in a single session three times, he said: 'It is one [divorce].'
ai.seo_question: Does pronouncing three divorces at once count as three or one in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential principle of 'counting' (i'tibar) in triple talaq, establishing that simultaneous pronouncements in a single state of purity constitute only one revocable divorce rather than three. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between 'talaq al-sunna' and 'talaq al-bid'ah', emphasizing that the divorce is not final until the waiting period (iddah) concludes. The hadith underscores the importance of the husband's intent and the specific conditions of purity in determining the validity of the divorce.
